significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, across specified scientific laws, a physical variable maps "monotonically and log-linearly onto a low-dimensional representational axis," with axis slope tracking the law's exponent and exponent distortion predicting extrapolation error; this constrains expected geometry across variable ranges, layers, and dimensionally equivalent inputs rather than merely showing decodability. This would establish a quantitative representational phenomenon and a candidate diagnostic, but not a causal mechanism showing that the axis produces model predictions; work such as AI Feynman (Udrescu and Tegmark, 2020) illustrates why dimensional and scaling constraints can materially delimit scientific generalization. The numerical core is determinate, whereas the phrase "true scientific understanding versus curve-fitting" is not; a negative result would rule out the proposed low-dimensional linear geometry but would not exclude nonlinear or distributed internalization, so that branch is only moderately informative. In the topic-substitution check, generic probing of scientific concepts would merit about 5, while the exponent, dimensional-equivalence, and extrapolation coupling—details false of the median topic claim—support the higher score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Scaling Fidelity Score," the "dimensional-consistency test," and the proposed link between "internal exponent distortion" and out-of-distribution extrapolation errors. If that predictive link is verified, these are ex-ante handles: an auditor could measure exponent fidelity before relying on a model outside its training range, leaving an action window to gate or reject its use. Although axes must be re-extracted for each model, the transferable conclusion predicts what should recur—agreement with the textbook exponent, shared subspaces for dimensionally equivalent variables, and lower reliability when fidelity degrades—rather than supplying only a procedure for searching; the asserted scope spans foundation models "for biology, chemistry, and materials," while appropriately remaining law- and model-specific. The downstream users include scientific-model auditors and builders, and the topic-substitution check lowers a generic representation probe to the median; the transferable quantitative audit and prospective reliability signal, not the importance of scientific modeling itself, justify the score.
